newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Monday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Monday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Monday:

Spokesman Peter Guilford briefed on the General Affairs Council's trade issues. He said the ministers had welcomed the Commisson's negotiations with Russia and Canada on the abolition of leghold traps and had asked to resume contacts to adapt the agreement on the basis of the EU presidency's ideas. He said these ideas were related notably to the date of the phase-out of certain kinds of trap, the possiblity of arbitration if countries do not obey the terms of the agreement and the way indigenous tribes could be given a derogation from the terms of the agreement.
Guilford said the Council had encouraged the EU to seek a bilateral solution with the U.S. on their dispute over the Helms-Burton law.
Guilford also said the ministers would discuss human rights in China at lunchtime but that there was no written proposal on this issue.

In answer to a question, spokesman Willy Helin said the Commission was unlikely to grant an exemption to a rule under which the banking industry forces shops not to discriminate between means of payment.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/48: Commissioner Karel Van Miert gives green light to licensing arrangement concluded between Cadbury Schweppes plc. and Coca-Cola Enterprises Inc.
- Speech/97/40: Speech by Commissioner Franz Fischler on the process of EU enlargement and a common environmental policy.
- Speech/97/41: Speech by Commission President Jacques Santer on "The EU currency as a chance for Europe.
- Speech/97/42: Speech by Commission President Jacques Santer on "A time for vision - a time for partnership".
